## Intent
When an employee cancels a leave request that was already SUBMITTED or APPROVED, the manager who would have decided it (or did decide it) must be notified, because today only the requester learns about a cancellation and an approver can be left holding a decision on a request that no longer exists.

Scope: on cancellation of a SUBMITTED or APPROVED request, send one notification to the approver — for an APPROVED request that is the recorded approverId; for a SUBMITTED one it is the requester's direct manager. A DRAFT cancellation notifies nobody, matching the existing rule that a DRAFT cancellation touches no balance. The notification must carry the request id and the leave type so the approver can act without a second lookup, and it must be sent inside the same unit of work as the status change, so a failure to notify cannot leave a cancelled request with no record of the notification attempt.

## Intent
When an employee cancels a leave request that was already SUBMITTED or APPROVED, the manager who would have decided it (or did decide it) must be notified, because today only the requester learns about a cancellation and an approver can be left holding a decision on a request that no longer exists.

Scope: on cancellation of a SUBMITTED or APPROVED request, send one notification to the approver — for an APPROVED request that is the recorded approverId; for a SUBMITTED one it is the requester's direct manager. A DRAFT cancellation notifies nobody, matching the existing rule that a DRAFT cancellation touches no balance. The notification must carry the request id and the leave type so the approver can act without a second lookup, and it must be sent inside the same unit of work as the status change, so a failure to notify cannot leave a cancelled request with no record of the notification attempt.

Also expose the approver's own view: GET /leaves/pending-decisions must stop listing a request once it is cancelled.

Keep the existing audit entry for a cancellation unchanged.

## Intent
When an employee cancels a leave request that was already SUBMITTED or APPROVED, the manager who would have decided it (or did decide it) must be notified, because today only the requester learns about a cancellation and an approver can be left holding a decision on a request that no longer exists.

Scope: on cancellation of a SUBMITTED or APPROVED request, send one notification to the approver — for an APPROVED request that is the recorded approverId; for a SUBMITTED one it is the requester's direct manager. A DRAFT cancellation notifies nobody, matching the existing rule that a DRAFT cancellation touches no balance. The notification must carry the request id and the leave type so the approver can act without a second lookup, and it must be sent inside the same unit of work as the status change, so a failure to notify cannot leave a cancelled request with no record of the notification attempt.

Also expose the approver's own view: GET /leaves/pending-decisions must stop listing a request once it is cancelled.
